studies.officialTitle: A Phase 1/2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Multiple-ascending-dose Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics of MEDI0382 in Overweight and Obese Subjects With a History of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

design.description: Six sequential multiple-ascending-dose cohorts with once-daily subcutaneous cotadutide.

studies.population: Adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes.
studies.overallDuration: 7 to 41 days of treatment, depending on cohort
studies.safetySummary: In the peer-reviewed Phase 2a portion, treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 88% of both groups. Gastrointestinal events were more frequent with cotadutide; no cotadutide recipient had a grade 3 or worse event, and there were no deaths.

design.masking: Triple-blind for cotadutide and placebo; open-label active comparator
design.description: Five-arm dose-ranging study on background metformin with three cotadutide doses, placebo, and liraglutide.

studies.population: Adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes treated with metformin.
studies.safetySummary: The fully reviewed 54-week report identified gastrointestinal disorders, including nausea and vomiting, as the most common events and reported that their event rates decreased over time. Three deaths occurred and none was considered treatment related; exact per-arm named safety outcomes remain unavailable because the supporting tables were not included with the public article.

design.description: Two-arm energy-balance study with a 16-day placebo run-in and 42-day double-blind treatment period.

studies.safetySummary: Most adverse events were mild or moderate. Four cotadutide recipients discontinued permanently because of adverse events; the publication reports nausea and vomiting among the most frequent events but leaves the exact per-arm named-event table in unavailable Supporting Information Table S7.
